title: Tube acceleration after first collision
description: Essential: Correctly states the tube's acceleration magnitude as 2g immediately after the first collision.

title: Ball acceleration after first collision
description: Essential: Correctly states the ball's acceleration magnitude as 3g immediately after the first collision.

title: Maximum height after first rebound
description: Essential: Correctly calculates the maximum height the tube reaches after the first bounce as (13/25)H.

title: Minimum tube length condition
description: Essential: Correctly derives the condition for the tube length L as L ≥ (152/125)H.

title: Applying Newton's second law
description: Important: Applies Newton's second law separately to the tube and ball after the first collision, using the given frictional force.

title: Velocity before first impact
description: Important: Correctly uses kinematics (v₀ = √(2gH)) to find the speed of tube and ball just before the first ground collision.

title: Relative motion analysis
description: Important: Analyzes the relative motion between ball and tube after a bounce to find the relative displacement (e.g., x₁ = 4H/5).

title: Energy or kinematics for height
description: Important: Uses energy methods or kinematics correctly to find the tube's maximum height after the first rebound.

title: Sign error in accelerations
description: Pitfall: Assigns incorrect signs or directions to the accelerations of the tube or ball after the collision.

title: Ignoring relative displacement sum
description: Pitfall: Fails to sum the relative displacements from the first and second rebounds (x₁ + x₂) for the length condition.
